question.leadin: Ozan Kilinc ("KILL-inch") was jailed by a court in this country for publishing articles sympathetic to a banned party.
question.text: Name this country, where insulting the country or the government is illegal under Article 301.
question.clue: The Simav and Nilufer Rivers flow into its Sea of Marmara.

swap.leadin: The Golden Horn cuts into this city and was once spanned by a large chain to prevent enemy ships from getting in.
swap.text: Name this Turkish city that was previously named Byzantium and Constantinople.
swap.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

question.leadin: A huge amount of impressive building projects were designed by this ruler's architect, Sinan.
question.text: Name this son of Selim the Grim, who won the Battle of Mohacs [Moe-HOTCH] but was less successful in conquering Malta and also led an unsuccessful siege of Vienna.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [or Suleiman the Lawgiver or Suleiman I; prompt on “Suleiman”]
question.clue: A principle known as the "circle of justice" guided the legal kanuns which he set up, and he supported the ascension of John Zapolya following one of his military victories.

swap.text: In the 1910s and 20s, the Young Turks perpetrated a genocide on this ethnic group, in which the Ottoman Empire forced this group from their homeland. The modern Turkish government refuses to identify the event as a genocide.
swap.answerHtml: Armenians (accept Armenian genocide or Armenian Holocaust, but do not prompt on Holocaust)
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.leadin: Many of those who orchestrated this event were assassinated during Operation Nemesis.
question.text: Identify this event in which over a million people of a certain Caucasian nationality were forcibly resettled and killed, perpetrated by the Ottoman Empire during World War I.
question.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide (accept equivalents like Armenian Massacre; prompt on “Great Crime” or “Medz Yeghern”)
question.clue: Discussion of it is suppressed today by Article 301, which has led to the persecution of Hrant Dink and Orhan Pamuk.

swap.text: This period of modernization, especially of the millet system, ended when Abdulhamid issued the First Ottoman Constitution.
swap.clue: This period of reform in the Ottoman Empire begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. This period included the abolition of the millet system and the elimination of tax farming.

question.text: The Janissaries were disbanded before this period of 19th-century reforms, which began with the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. Its modernizing provisions included ending a tax on non-Muslims and nationalizing the census.
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.text: You probably know that the Ottomans lost at the Battle of Lepanto, but more damaging was the increasing cost of employing these mostly-Christian infantrymen, recruited through the devshirme system.
swap.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

question.leadin: He died at the siege of Szigetvar after resuming warfare in Hungary in 1566.
question.text: Name this Ottoman sultan, the son of Selim the Grim, who defeated the aforementioned Hungarians at the great battle of Mohacs forty years earlier.
question.clue: He employed Sinan as the chief architect, married Roxelana, and was often called "kanuni."

swap.text: This Ottoman Sultan, the last to acutally control the Empire, succeeded Murad V and was overthrown by the Young Turks. He conscripted Kurdish to crush Armenian uprising like the Sasun Resistance in his namesake massacres.
swap.clue: The second ruler of this name moved his seat of government to Yildiz Palace.

question.leadin: It was the first campaign fought by the combined New Zealand-Australian forces called ANZAC.
question.text: Name this campaign of 1915 into early 1916 in which the British and French attempted to capture Istanbul by taking a certain peninsula in Turkey.
question.answerHtml: Gallipoli Campaign [or Dardanelles Campaign; or Çanakkale Savaşları; or Çanakkale Wars]
question.clue: William Birdwood coordinated his attack on Hill 60 with another assault on Scimitar Hill during this campaign, though both offensives failed.

swap.text: This July 1923 Treaty saw Greek gains from Sevres transferred to the new nation of Turkey. AJanuary 1923 convention signed in the same Swiss town saw the forced population transfer of 2 million Muslims and Christians between Greece and Turkey.
swap.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

question.text: In 1845, a holder of this title wrote the treatise "Benefits to Children" describing vaccine efforts for a cowpox outbreak. Holders of this Ottoman title like Enver and Cemal ["jamal"] led a "Young Turk Triumvirate" shadow government until the empire's collapse post-WWI.
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the decline of the "sick man of Europe," a.k.a. the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: The beginning of the Ottomans' downfall is often traced to this 1699 treaty, which transferred Hungary and Transylvania to Austria's control.
swap.clue: Its Russian portion was supplemented in the following year by a treaty which transferred Azov, and it exempted an area defined by the Tisza, Mures, and Danube rivers, the Banat of Temesvar, from one provision.

question.leadin: These people established trading posts in Anatolia called karum, including at the site of Kultepe (cull-TEH-pay).
question.text: Name these people who lost much of their commercial influence after Hammurabi defeated their king Ishme-Dagan, the son of these people's powerful king Shamshi-Adad I ("the first").
question.clue: These people amusingly celebrate New Years' on April 1st with a festival called Kha b-Nisan.

swap.text: This was the highest position a Devshirme could achieve. This most important minister was dismissible only by the Sultan and held the imperial seal.
swap.answerHtml: Grand Vizier [accept Vezir-i Azam, Sadr-i Azam, or Sadrazam; prompt on vizier]

question.leadin: Name these units of the Ottoman Army.
question.text: The least prestigious unit of the Ottoman military consisted of these irregular, unprofessional soldiers. Their name translates to "damaged head", a reference to their lack of discipline.
question.clue: This irregular Ottoman troops whose Turkish name means "disorderly heads" in reference to their tendency to loot. Gladstone's Midlothian campaign denounced these units' involvement in the "Bulgarian horrors."

swap.leadin: This Italian converted to Islam after being captured by corsairs, eventually becoming the Pasha of Algiers with the help of Selim II.
swap.text: Name this man who commanded the left flank of a fleet whose overall command went to Muezzinzade Ali Pasha.
swap.answerHtml: Uluj Ali [accept Uluç Ali Reis; accept Uluç Ali Paşa; accept Kılıç Ali Paşa; accept Giovanni Dionigi Galeni]

question.text: This overall commander of Ottoman forces at Beersheba later received a surname drawn from the two 1921 battles where he forced invading Greeks to retreat. He was the successor of Ataturk as the second President of Turkey.
question.clue: The implementer of the Turkish surname law, Mustafa Kemal, took the surname Ataturk, while this "National Chief" who succeeded him took his surname from a town where he fought during the Greco-Turkish War.

swap.leadin: Name these groups of Europeans within the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: The Cantacuino and Ypsilanti families were part of this class of leading residents of Constantinople's Greek quarter. They were the namesake of the eighteenth century in Romanian history because they were appointed as hospodars there, and they controlled the selection of the Orthodox patriarch.
swap.clue: In the 18th century, this class of Greek merchant families dominated Ottoman government positions such as Grand Dragoman of the Fleet and Hospodar of Moldavia. They were named after a Greek neighborhood in Istanbul.
